The tiers buy memory at no cost to accuracy; the accuracy comes from keeping momentum, which a uniform optimizer shares too. Sweeping the baselines' learning rates narrows but does not close the gap: the best tuned AdamW reaches 118.5, tuned Adafactor 139.7. Where optimizer state lives, these results suggest, matters at least as much as how much of it there is.

AI.tldr: SkewAdam reduces MoE optimizer memory from 50.6 GB to 1.29 GB (2.6% of AdamW) by assigning different optimizer states to backbone (float32 momentum + factored second moment), experts (factored second moment only), and router (exact second moment), achieving lower perplexity (108.4 vs AdamW's 126.8) while fitting in 40 GB memory.
AI.motivation: Optimizer state dominates memory in MoE training (50.6 GB for AdamW on a 6.78B MoE), and the three parameter populations (backbone, experts, router) differ significantly in size and gradient statistics, suggesting they should not share the same optimizer state allocation.
AI.method: SkewAdam assigns tiered optimizer states: float32 momentum + factored second moment for the dense backbone (5% of params), factored second moment alone for experts (95%), and exact second moment for the router (<0.01%), leveraging the observation that momentum is crucial for accuracy while memory can be saved where it doesn't hurt performance.
AI.result: Peak memory drops from 81.4 GB to 31.3 GB (fitting in 40 GB accelerator). SkewAdam achieves validation perplexity 108.4 vs AdamW 126.8, Muon 120.2, Lion 393.7. Router load balance within 1% of uniform floor. Tier ablation matches with 20x state; Adafactor (no momentum) plateaus 40 points behind.
AI.conclusion: Where optimizer state is allocated matters at least as much as how much of it exists; momentum is critical for accuracy, and the tiered approach buys memory savings without sacrificing quality.

title: Deep learning-based prediction of time-resolved adhesive forces in viscoelastic Hertzian contacts
summary: Fast prediction of the response of adhesive soft viscoelastic contacts represents a current challenge in soft robotics and for gripping and manipulation tasks. Determining the complete time-resolved force trajectory requires full numerical simulations, whose computational cost is strongly parameter-dependent, making them impractical for real-time application or design-optimization loops. In this work, we overcome this limitation by training a scalar-conditioned, stateful, sequence-to-sequence deep learning model to predict the full force evolution from a prescribed displacement history for both short- and long-range adhesion regimes. The data set spans four orders of magnitude in loading and unloading rates and includes varied dwell times, with the Tabor parameter ranging from $0.2$ to $3.2$. To enable learning across these heterogeneous time scales, we introduce a fixed-measurement-step (FMS) representation that converts variable-length trajectories into fixed-length sequences while preserving their physical-time information. Different architectures were trained, including long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, temporal convolutional neural (TCN) networks, and time-distributed dense layers with three different Tabor-conditioning mechanisms. The models were compared using global waveform and error metrics. We found that the best-performing model has an LSTM architecture with concatenated conditioning, which achieves a held-out mean-squared error of $5.0\times10^{-4}$, a median pull-off-force error of $\approx2.2\%$, and a median hysteresis error of $\approx1.1\%$. For the held-out protocols, the model predicts a complete force trajectory with a median inference time of $0.16$ s. The model is tested across unseen parameter combinations and against analytical limiting cases, providing a rapid surrogate for repeated numerical evaluations with potential use in control-oriented applications.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a deep learning model (LSTM with concatenated conditioning) that predicts full force-evolution trajectories for adhesive soft viscoelastic contacts from prescribed displacement histories, achieving high accuracy (MSE 5.0×10⁻⁴, median pull-off force error ~2.2%) with rapid inference (0.16 s), across four orders of magnitude in loading rates and a range of Tabor parameters (0.2–3.2).
AI.motivation: Fast prediction of adhesive soft viscoelastic contact response is a current challenge in soft robotics and gripping/manipulation tasks; full numerical simulations are computationally expensive and parameter-dependent, making them impractical for real-time applications or design optimization.
AI.method: A scalar-conditioned, stateful, sequence-to-sequence deep learning model was trained on data spanning four orders of magnitude in loading/unloading rates and varied dwell times (Tabor parameter 0.2–3.2). A fixed-measurement-step (FMS) representation converts variable-length trajectories into fixed-length sequences. Multiple architectures were compared: LSTM networks, temporal convolutional neural networks (TCN), and time-distributed dense layers with three Tabor-conditioning mechanisms.
AI.result: The best model (LSTM with concatenated conditioning) achieved held-out MSE of 5.0×10⁻⁴, median pull-off-force error ≈2.2%, median hysteresis error ≈1.1%, and median inference time of 0.16 s per trajectory. The model was tested on unseen parameter combinations and analytical limiting cases.
AI.conclusion: The deep learning surrogate provides rapid, accurate predictions of full force trajectories for adhesive viscoelastic contacts, enabling potential use in control-oriented applications and design-optimization loops where repeated numerical evaluations are needed.

title: GEqTrain: A Configuration-Driven Framework for Retargeting Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Across 3D Scientific Tasks
summary: Equivariant graph neural networks provide a powerful modeling language for three-dimensional scientific data, but their reuse is often limited by implementations tied to specific tasks, outputs, and training regimes. We present GEqTrain, a configuration-driven framework that separates dataset semantics, model composition, and training objectives. Raw data are mapped to typed node-, edge-, and graph-level fields, while model stacks, losses, and training workflows are assembled declaratively through Hydra configurations. A shared equivariant backbone and training infrastructure can therefore be retargeted to a new task primarily through configuration. We demonstrate this flexibility on three different problems handled within one software stack: coarse-grained-to-atomistic backmapping of biomolecular systems, prediction of NMR chemical shifts in molecular solids, and equivariant generative modeling. Our aim is not to surpass individually optimized task-specific systems, but to show that a shared representation and training infrastructure can achieve competitive accuracy across qualitatively different tasks at the cost of a configuration change. We further introduce GEqDiff, a generative extension based on equivariant flow matching. GEqDiff treats user-defined equivariant fields as first-class generation targets, jointly transporting Cartesian positions and non-scalar node fields spanning representations up to l=3 within a single equivariant flow. We validate this capability on a controlled synthetic benchmark inspired by protein secondary-structure motifs, showing that fields with heterogeneous transformation properties can be reconstructed jointly and with high fidelity. By reducing the software overhead of moving between predictive and generative, scalar and tensorial settings, GEqTrain aims to make equivariant modeling more reproducible, extensible, and reusable.

AI.tldr: GEqTrain is a configuration-driven framework for equivariant graph neural networks that separates dataset semantics, model composition, and training objectives, enabling reuse across different tasks (backmapping, NMR shift prediction, generative modeling) via configuration changes. It also introduces GEqDiff, a generative extension using equivariant flow matching to jointly transport Cartesian positions and non-scalar node fields up to l=3.
AI.motivation: Equivariant GNN implementations are often tied to specific tasks, outputs, and training regimes, limiting reuse and reproducibility. The authors aim to reduce software overhead when moving between predictive and generative, scalar and tensorial settings.
AI.method: GEqTrain uses Hydra configurations to declaratively assemble model stacks, losses, and training workflows. Raw data are mapped to typed node-, edge-, and graph-level fields. GEqDiff extends this with equivariant flow matching, treating user-defined equivariant fields as first-class generation targets.
AI.result: Demonstrated on three tasks (coarse-grained-to-atomistic backmapping, NMR chemical shift prediction, equivariant generative modeling) within one software stack. GEqDiff validated on a synthetic benchmark inspired by protein secondary-structure motifs, showing high-fidelity joint reconstruction of fields with heterogeneous transformation properties.
AI.conclusion: A shared representation and training infrastructure can achieve competitive accuracy across qualitatively different tasks primarily through configuration changes. GEqTrain aims to make equivariant modeling more reproducible, extensible, and reusable.

title: An unsupervised clustering analysis of breast cancer data derived from electronic health records enhanced through UMAP dimensionality reduction
comment: Accepted at the CIBB 2026 conference ( https://cibb2026.teralab.ai/ )
summary: Breast cancer is one of the most widespread types of cancer, affecting approximately 8 million women worldwide. Electronic health records of patients diagnosed with this disease can serve as valuable datasets for computational analyses, enabling the discovery of new insights about the pathology. Unsupervised clustering, in particular, can identify groups of patients with medically significant features, revealing data trends that might otherwise go unnoticed by medical doctors. In this study, we first applied the DBSCAN density-based clustering method to three independent datasets derived from electronic medical records of patients with mammary carcinoma. Subsequently, to enhance our results, we preceded the DBSCAN application with a dimensionality reduction phase using UMAP. We evaluated our clustering outcomes using three statistical indices (DBCV, DCSI, and DISCO). Our results confirm the effectiveness of combining UMAP with DBSCAN for clustering data derived from electronic health records, paving the way for the medical interpretation of the patient groups identified by our approach.

AI.tldr: This study applies DBSCAN clustering with UMAP dimensionality reduction to electronic health records of breast cancer patients, demonstrating improved clustering effectiveness across three datasets validated by three statistical indices.
AI.motivation: Breast cancer affects ~8 million women worldwide, and electronic health records contain valuable but complex data. Unsupervised clustering can reveal medically meaningful patient subgroups that might go unnoticed manually, motivating the need for effective clustering methods on such data.
AI.method: The authors applied DBSCAN density-based clustering to three independent breast cancer EHR datasets, first alone and then preceded by UMAP dimensionality reduction. Clustering quality was evaluated using three indices: DBCV, DCSI, and DISCO.
AI.result: The combination of UMAP with DBSCAN outperformed DBSCAN alone in clustering effectiveness across all three datasets, as confirmed by the three statistical evaluation indices.
AI.conclusion: UMAP + DBSCAN is an effective pipeline for clustering electronic health record data of breast cancer patients, enabling identification of interpretable patient subgroups for further medical analysis.

title: Predicting Activities in Aqueous Electrolyte Solutions with Hybrid Machine Learning
summary: Activities in aqueous electrolyte solutions, usually described by ionic activity and osmotic coefficients, are important properties for modeling many processes in industry and nature. Established activity models, such as those of Pitzer or Bromley, require fitting to experimental data for each electrolyte of interest and thus cannot predict properties for unstudied systems. While some predictive approaches exist, they are typically limited in scope and rely on additional ion-specific descriptors. In this work, we introduce a new hybrid model that combines the physics-based Bromley model with a matrix completion method (MCM) from machine learning. The MCM is employed to predict the electrolyte-specific parameters of the Bromley model, exploiting the fact that these parameters can be arranged in a matrix with cations and anions as rows and columns, respectively. Due to the lack of experimental data for many electrolytes, the initial parameter matrix is sparsely populated, making the prediction of the Bromley parameters for unstudied electrolytes a matrix completion problem. The hybrid model, Bromley-MCM, was trained end-to-end on experimental data for mean ionic activity coefficients and osmotic coefficients of aqueous solutions of 478 electrolytes at 298 K from the Dortmund Data Bank. As output, we obtain a completed matrix of Bromley parameters for 83 cations and 112 anions, enabling consistent prediction of concentration-dependent activities in aqueous solutions of 9,296 electrolytes at 298~K. This substantially extends the applicability of the Bromley model while maintaining high predictive accuracy, as demonstrated through evaluations on electrolytes excluded from model training.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Bromley-MCM, a hybrid model combining the physics-based Bromley model with matrix completion (machine learning) to predict activity and osmotic coefficients for aqueous electrolyte solutions. It fills missing Bromley parameters for unstudied electrolytes, extending predictions to 9,296 electrolytes at 298 K while maintaining high accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing activity models (e.g., Pitzer, Bromley) require experimental fitting for each electrolyte and cannot predict properties for unstudied systems. Predictive approaches that do exist are limited in scope and rely on additional ion-specific descriptors, motivating the need for a more generalizable method.
AI.method: The authors combine the physics-based Bromley model with a matrix completion method (MCM) from machine learning. Bromley parameters are arranged in a cation-by-anion matrix; due to missing experimental data, predicting parameters for unstudied electrolytes becomes a matrix completion problem. The hybrid Bromley-MCM model is trained end-to-end on mean ionic activity coefficients and osmotic coefficients for 478 electrolytes from the Dortmund Data Bank at 298 K.
AI.result: The model outputs a completed matrix of Bromley parameters for 83 cations and 112 anions, enabling consistent prediction for 9,296 electrolytes at 298 K. High predictive accuracy is demonstrated via evaluations on electrolytes excluded from training, substantially extending the Bromley model's applicability.
AI.conclusion: The Bromley-MCM hybrid model successfully extends the Bromley model to a large, unstudied set of electrolytes without requiring additional ion-specific descriptors, maintaining high predictive accuracy and offering a scalable solution for predicting electrolyte solution thermodynamics.

title: Parallel Noising in Neural Markov Logic Networks
summary: Neural Markov Logic Networks (NMLNs) are a flexible neurosymbolic relational model. Previous work has shown that, although NMLNs achieve strong performance as generative models for small relational structures, they underperform diffusion-based generative graph models on larger structures. In this paper, we strengthen NMLNs along two main dimensions: (i) we increase the expressive capacity of their potential functions using graph neural networks, and (ii) we develop a new training and inference algorithm inspired by parallel-tempering Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, which we name parallel noising. Together, these enhancements enable NMLNs to attain strong performance in graph generation relative to general diffusion-based generative graph models. Furthermore, they allow NMLNs to match the performance of specialized text-based recurrent models when generating small molecular structures.

AI.tldr: The paper enhances Neural Markov Logic Networks (NMLNs) with graph neural network potentials and a parallel noising training/inference algorithm, enabling them to perform competitively with diffusion-based graph models on large structures and match specialized models on molecular generation.
AI.motivation: Previous NMLNs underperform compared to diffusion-based generative graph models on larger relational structures, motivating the need for architectural and algorithmic improvements.
AI.method: (i) Increasing expressive capacity of potential functions using graph neural networks; (ii) Developing a new training and inference algorithm called parallel noising, inspired by parallel-tempering MCMC.
AI.result: Enhanced NMLNs attain strong performance in graph generation relative to diffusion-based models, and match specialized text-based recurrent models on small molecular structure generation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed enhancements successfully bridge the performance gap between NMLNs and state-of-the-art generative graph models across both large and small relational structures.

title: One Model, Many Graphs: Learning over Attributed Graphs across Heterogeneous Modalities with Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) provide a unified representation space for textual and visual information, yet their potential as general-purpose backbones for graph-structured data remains largely unexplored. In practice, attributed graphs exhibit substantial modality heterogeneity: some graphs contain only textual node attributes, others only visual attributes, while still others provide both. Existing graph learning approaches are typically designed for fixed modality schemas, requiring separate models for different settings and limiting scalability and cross-graph generalization. To bridge this gap, we present OMG-VLM (One Model, Many Graphs with Vision-Language Models), a unified framework for learning over attributed graphs across heterogeneous modality schemas. OMG-VLM leverages a pretrained VLM as a shared backbone and introduces structure-aware graph adapters that integrate neighborhood information while remaining compatible with the VLM's native embedding space. This design enables effective learning over text-attributed, image-attributed, and multi-attributed graphs within a single model. Extensive experiments across diverse domains show that OMG-VLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art GNN- and LLM-based baselines on attributed graph learning tasks such as node classification and link prediction, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen graphs and varying modality schemas. The source code is available at https://github.com/Jo-eyang/OMG-VLM.

AI.tldr: OMG-VLM is a unified framework that leverages a pretrained vision-language model as a shared backbone with structure-aware graph adapters to handle attributed graphs with heterogeneous modality schemas (text-only, image-only, or both), outperforming GNN- and LLM-based baselines on node classification and link prediction.
AI.motivation: Existing graph learning approaches are designed for fixed modality schemas, requiring separate models for text-attributed, image-attributed, or multi-attributed graphs, limiting scalability and cross-graph generalization. Vision-language models' potential as general-purpose backbones for graph-structured data remains unexplored.
AI.method: OMG-VLM uses a pretrained VLM as a shared backbone, augmented with structure-aware graph adapters that integrate neighborhood information while remaining compatible with the VLM's native embedding space, enabling a single model to handle text-only, image-only, and multi-attributed graphs.
AI.result: OMG-VLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art GNN- and LLM-based baselines on node classification and link prediction across diverse domains, and exhibits strong generalization to unseen graphs and varying modality schemas.
AI.conclusion: A single pretrained VLM backbone with structure-aware graph adapters can serve as a unified and generalizable solution for attributed graph learning across heterogeneous modality schemas, eliminating the need for separate models per modality setting.

title: Incomplete Observations Boost Evolutionary Performance in Ocean Modeling
summary: Data-driven methods have revolutionized ocean modeling, yet current approaches rely heavily on complete reanalysis datasets, imposing computational constraints and limiting model performance to that of the training data. Here, we present a generative state-space model and an optimization framework that enable learning directly from sparse and noisy observations. The model is essentially a hidden Markov model with a continuous state space, where oceanic physical quantities are treated as hidden states and measurements as observations, enabling a unified representation of ocean fields and observational data. Both the initial-state and state-transition modules are implemented as neural networks to capture the complexity and temporal evolution of ocean states, while the emission module is formulated as a masked Gaussian distribution. To train the model from sparse observations, we derive an optimization framework based on the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm. The framework alternately reconstructs high-fidelity ocean fields via Langevin dynamics and optimizes deep neural networks to capture temporal evolution. Theoretical analysis shows that the framework maximizes the likelihood of observations under the generative model. For efficiency, we assume that ocean-state evolution follows a stationary, ergodic, and Markovian stochastic process and adopt only length-two state sequences during optimization. Experiments on CMIP6 simulation data and FY-3D satellite data demonstrate high-fidelity reconstruction and accurate prediction, showing that sparse observations can directly improve the model's representation of ocean-state dynamics. This work offers a scalable pathway for next-generation Earth system models to learn directly from sparse, incomplete real-world observations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a generative state-space model (hidden Markov model with neural networks) and an EM-based optimization framework that learns ocean dynamics directly from sparse, noisy observations, achieving high-fidelity reconstruction and prediction without requiring complete reanalysis datasets.
AI.motivation: Current data-driven ocean modeling relies on complete reanalysis datasets, which imposes computational constraints and limits model performance to that of the training data. The authors aim to overcome this bottleneck by enabling learning directly from sparse and noisy observations.
AI.method: A generative state-space model (continuous-state hidden Markov model) where ocean states are hidden and measurements are observations. The initial-state and state-transition modules are neural networks; the emission module is a masked Gaussian distribution. Training uses an EM algorithm framework that alternates between reconstructing ocean fields via Langevin dynamics and optimizing DNNs, assuming stationary, ergodic, Markovian ocean evolution with length-two state sequences for efficiency.
AI.result: Experiments on CMIP6 simulation data and FY-3D satellite data demonstrate high-fidelity reconstruction and accurate prediction. Sparse observations directly improve the model's representation of ocean-state dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The work offers a scalable pathway for next-generation Earth system models to learn directly from sparse, incomplete real-world observations, bypassing the need for complete reanalysis datasets.

title: Breaking the Homogeneity Assumption: Specialized Multi-Generator Adversarial Learning for Rare Failure Detection in Predictive Maintenance
summary: Supervised learning models in the predictive maintenance field are regularly trained on highly imbalanced industrial datasets: machine failures occur rarely but have a disproportionate effect on operations. In addition to the clear class disparity, failure data are typically non-homogeneous, with different failure modes arising from distinct physical processes and exhibiting a multimodal distribution across minorities and classes. Traditional imbalance-management methods, e.g., undersampling, SMOTE-based interpolation, or cost-sensitive learning, typically assume that the minority population is homogeneous. This means their effectiveness is severely limited in the multifaceted conditions encountered in industrial practice. This paper determines the possibility of a failure-type-conscious generative augmentation program to improve the identification of infrequent failures in predictive maintenance systems. An experimental design that is leakage-safe is used to compare five imbalance-handling methods: cost-sensitive learning, random undersampling, SMOTE oversampling, single-generator GAN augmentation, and a specialized multi-generator GAN architecture that has independent generators that are asked to learn individual failure subtypes. Precision/Recall-oriented measures are used to quantify model performance; the main evaluation measure is the PR-AUC. Experiments conducted on the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset indicate that the proposed multi-generator GAN framework produces more realistic minority samples, yielding higher PR-AUC and recall scores compared to traditional resampling methods and individual-generator GAN augmentation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a multi-generator GAN architecture for handling non-homogeneous minority class distributions in imbalanced predictive maintenance datasets, outperforming traditional imbalance methods by generating failure-type-conscious synthetic samples.
AI.motivation: Supervised learning in predictive maintenance suffers from highly imbalanced datasets where failures are rare, non-homogeneous, and multimodal across classes. Traditional imbalance methods assume homogeneous minority populations, limiting their effectiveness in complex industrial settings.
AI.method: A multi-generator GAN framework where independent generators learn individual failure subtypes; compared against cost-sensitive learning, random undersampling, SMOTE oversampling, and single-generator GAN augmentation using a leakage-safe experimental design.
AI.result: The multi-generator GAN produced more realistic minority samples and achieved higher PR-AUC and recall scores than traditional resampling methods and single-generator GAN on the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset.
AI.conclusion: Failure-type-conscious generative augmentation effectively improves identification of infrequent failures in predictive maintenance, with the multi-generator GAN being superior for non-homogeneous minority class distributions.

title: Neural Kolmogorov Equations: Parallelizable Learning of Stochastic Dynamics under General Noise
summary: Neural stochastic differential equations (SDEs) have emerged as powerful tools for learning noisy or stochastic dynamics directly from data; however, existing approaches largely assume uncoupled and continuous noise, limiting their applicability to realistic stochastic drivers, and often scale poorly in time, requiring expensive autoregressive training. To address these limitations, we propose Neural Kolmogorov Equations (NKEs), a deterministic, infinite-dimensional reformulation of Neural SDEs based on the Kolmogorov Forward equation, transforming the learning problem from modelling individual stochastic trajectories to modelling the evolution of probability densities. NKEs learn general Lévy-type stochastic forcing directly through the operator structure of the KFE, and enable parallel-in-time training via a Lagrangian Galerkin projection and operator splitting. We evaluate NKEs on several stochastic benchmarks, including systems with coupled noise and jump processes, and verify that NKEs provide flexible models that accurately recover deterministic and stochastic dynamics with competitive predictive accuracy and improved training efficiency. Code and pretrained models will be released.

AI.tldr: Neural Kolmogorov Equations (NKEs) reformulate Neural SDEs as deterministic density evolution via the Kolmogorov Forward Equation, enabling Lévy-type noise modeling and parallel-in-time training.
AI.motivation: Existing Neural SDEs assume uncoupled continuous noise, limiting applicability to realistic stochastic drivers, and scale poorly in time due to expensive autoregressive training.
AI.method: NKEs transform Neural SDEs into a deterministic infinite-dimensional problem using the Kolmogorov Forward Equation, model Lévy-type stochastic forcing via operator structure of KFE, and enable parallel-in-time training through Lagrangian Galerkin projection with operator splitting.
AI.result: NKEs accurately recover deterministic and stochastic dynamics, handle coupled noise and jump processes, achieve competitive predictive accuracy with improved training efficiency.
AI.conclusion: NKEs provide flexible, efficient models for learning stochastic dynamics with general noise structures, overcoming key limitations of Neural SDEs.

title: Conservative Query and Adaptive Regularization for Offline RL Under Uncertainty Estimation
summary: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn an effective policy from a static dataset, but its performance is fundamentally limited by dataset coverage. Action preference queries leverage expert feedback without additional environment interaction, enabling policy improvement during offline training. However, existing methods still face two key challenges: selecting informative preference queries and effectively exploiting the collected feedback. Current approaches typically rely only on the distance between policy actions and dataset actions for query selection, while enforcing fixed constraints that keep the policy close to queried preferences. Such strategies often lead to unstable policy updates and integrate poorly with value regularization. To address these limitations, we propose Conservative Query and Adaptive Regularization under Uncertainty Estimation, a lightweight framework that jointly improves preference querying and preference exploitation. Specifically, we employ a Morse network to estimate the uncertainty of policy actions with respect to the offline dataset. Based on this uncertainty, we introduce a conservative query strategy that selectively queries actions near the dataset to preserve Bellman-update stability, together with an uncertainty-aware adaptive regularization scheme that dynamically adjusts data-level constraints during policy optimization. We integrate our framework with CQL and evaluate it extensively on the D4RL benchmark. Experimental results demonstrate superior or competitive performance across a wide range of tasks.

AI.tldr: CQUAR proposes a lightweight framework using uncertainty estimation (via Morse network) to improve both action preference querying and adaptive regularization for offline RL, outperforming baselines on D4RL tasks.
AI.motivation: Offline RL performance is limited by dataset coverage. Existing action preference query methods suffer from unstable policy updates and poor integration with value regularization due to suboptimal query selection and fixed constraints.
AI.method: Uses a Morse network to estimate policy action uncertainty relative to offline dataset; introduces conservative query strategy that selectively queries actions near the dataset, and an uncertainty-aware adaptive regularization scheme that dynamically adjusts data-level constraints during policy optimization, integrated with CQL.
AI.result: Superior or competitive performance across a wide range of D4RL benchmark tasks compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Jointly improving preference querying and exploitation via uncertainty estimation effectively addresses instability and integration issues in offline RL with human feedback.

title: AdaFlash: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via On-Policy Distilled Diffusion Drafters
summary: Speculative decoding, in which a lightweight draft model first generates a draft sequence that is then verified in parallel by the target model, has become a prevalent paradigm for accelerating large language model inference. Recent work such as DFlash further boosts drafting efficiency by leveraging diffusion drafters, whose parallel denoising mechanism enables draft generation in a single forward pass. In this work, we uncover a central pitfall of diffusion drafters: bidirectional attention is a double-edged sword. On one hand, it endows the model with parallel generation and global contextual modeling capabilities; on the other hand, this inherent global dependency introduces high variance at both the domain-level and the token-level: acceptance rates fluctuate substantially across different domains, and draft token quality also varies heterogeneously at different token positions. To tackle this issue, we propose AdaFlash framework, comprising two components: (i) an on-policy distillation (OPD) algorithm with reverse-KL divergence tailored for diffusion drafters, bringing stable convergence and effectively reducing domain-level variance; and (ii) an adaptive length head that dynamically adjusts the candidate sequence length on the fly, substantially lowering the verification cost of the target model and handling token-level variance. Experiments demonstrate that AdaFlash consistently improves speedup rate during deployment, with especially significant gains in high-concurrency scenarios, achieving up to approximately 66% higher throughput than previous state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: AdaFlash addresses the bidirectional attention pitfalls in diffusion drafters for speculative decoding by introducing on-policy distillation with reverse-KL divergence and an adaptive length head, achieving up to ~66% higher throughput over prior SOTA.
AI.motivation: The authors uncover that bidirectional attention in diffusion drafters is a double-edged sword: it enables parallel generation and global context modeling but introduces high variance at both domain-level (fluctuating acceptance rates across domains) and token-level (heterogeneous draft token quality at different positions), limiting efficiency.
AI.method: AdaFlash proposes two components: (i) an on-policy distillation (OPD) algorithm with reverse-KL divergence tailored for diffusion drafters to reduce domain-level variance with stable convergence; (ii) an adaptive length head that dynamically adjusts candidate sequence length on the fly to reduce verification cost and handle token-level variance.
AI.result: AdaFlash consistently improves speedup during deployment, with especially significant gains in high-concurrency scenarios, achieving up to approximately 66% higher throughput than previous state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively mitigates the variance issues caused by bidirectional attention in diffusion drafters, making speculative decoding more robust and efficient, particularly under high concurrency.

title: S3: Stable Subgoal Selection by Constraining Uncertainty of Coarse Dynamics in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
comment: Manuscript accepted to the Eighteenth Workshop on Adaptive and Learning Agents (ALA), at the 25th International Conference of Autonomous Agents and Multi Agent Systems 2026
summary: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) intends to separate strategic planning from primitive execution. It has been widely successful in solving long-horizon and complex tasks, where flat-RL algorithms have difficulty in learning. However, while the low-level agent in HRL benefits from dense feedback and abundant trial opportunities, the high-level agent receives sparse, delayed feedback from the environment and its performance depends on the low-level execution capability. In this paper, we study whether subgoal selection by the high-level agent can be performed more strategically, by providing it with dynamics-aware intrinsic motivation. Since motivation based on primitive transition dynamics would require broad coverage of the state-action space, we propose to use coarse dynamics, i.e., environment transitions aggregated over multiple steps at the temporal scale at which the high-level agent operates. This approach stabilizes the high-level policy by learning to minimize the predictive uncertainty associated with the coarse dynamics, and provides a guided structure for navigation. We model the predictive uncertainty by evaluating different dispersion metrics as approximated by a Mixture Density Network (MDN). Empirically, we observe that a dense, dynamics-aware intrinsic reward leads to risk-averse subgoal selection, enabling it to outperform state-of-the-art HRL methods in non-stationary long-horizon environments.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a dynamics-aware intrinsic motivation mechanism for high-level agents in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning, using coarse dynamics and Mixture Density Networks to model predictive uncertainty, enabling more strategic and risk-averse subgoal selection that outperforms state-of-the-art HRL methods in non-stationary long-horizon tasks.
AI.motivation: In HRL, high-level agents receive sparse/delayed feedback and depend on low-level execution capability, making subgoal selection suboptimal. The paper aims to provide the high-level agent with strategic, dynamics-aware intrinsic motivation to improve its decision-making.
AI.method: The authors propose using coarse dynamics (environment transitions aggregated over multiple steps at the high-level temporal scale) to compute predictive uncertainty via Mixture Density Networks (MDN). This uncertainty serves as a dense intrinsic reward, guiding subgoal selection toward risk-averse behavior.
AI.result: The dense, dynamics-aware intrinsic reward leads to risk-averse subgoal selection and outperforms state-of-the-art HRL methods in non-stationary long-horizon environments.
AI.conclusion: Providing high-level agents with coarse dynamics-based intrinsic motivation stabilizes policy learning and improves performance in complex, long-horizon tasks where standard HRL struggles.

title: In-Context Time Series Classification with Random Convolutional Features
summary:
Time series classification is central to domains like medical signal analysis, industrial monitoring, and sensor-based activity recognition, where class information manifests as localized shapes, specific frequencies, temporal shifts, or complex cross-channel interactions. Random convolutional transforms efficiently map these sequences to fixed-dimensional tabular features but are traditionally paired with simple linear classifiers. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model can more effectively harness these rich representations.
  We propose MASHT, a pipeline that marries MultiRocket and Hydra features with the power of in-context tabular foundation models. By leveraging a pretrained tabular foundation model, our approach completely bypasses task-specific model training, requiring only feature extraction and direct inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MASHT matches state-of-the-art time series classification baselines on univariate tasks, achieving a lower average rank than HIVE-COTE 2.0. On multivariate datasets, MASHT remains highly competitive with the strongest reference methods.

AI.tldr: MASHT combines MultiRocket and Hydra features with a pretrained tabular foundation model, bypassing task-specific training, and achieves competitive or state-of-the-art time series classification performance on both univariate and multivariate datasets.
AI.motivation: Random convolutional transforms map time series to fixed-dimensional tabular features but are traditionally paired with simple linear classifiers. The authors investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model can more effectively harness these rich representations for time series classification.
AI.method: MASHT marries MultiRocket and Hydra features with a pretrained tabular foundation model, performing feature extraction followed by direct inference without any task-specific model training.
AI.result: MASHT matches state-of-the-art time series classification baselines on univariate tasks (lower average rank than HIVE-COTE 2.0) and remains highly competitive on multivariate datasets against the strongest reference methods.
AI.conclusion: Pretrained tabular foundation models can effectively replace traditional linear classifiers for random convolutional time series features, achieving competitive performance while completely bypassing task-specific training.

title: DBMol: Design of High-Affinity, Target-Specific Small Molecules through Structure Prediction Models
summary: Designing small molecule ligands that bind with high affinity to specific protein pockets is a fundamental goal in drug discovery, as small molecules constitute a major fraction of approved therapeutics. Recent breakthroughs in structure prediction, such as AlphaFold-3 and Boltz-2, enable accurate biomolecular interaction prediction and show promise as foundation models for downstream tasks, including binding affinity prediction. We propose to leverage these models and introduce DBMol, a new structure predictor-guided framework for de novo small molecule design. DBMol formulates an alternating optimization and projection process. In the optimization stage, DBMol starts from an initial molecule and uses gradient-based optimization to improve pocket-specific interactions and predicted binding affinity using a structure prediction model. In the projection stage, a flow-matching model maps the optimized molecular graph to discrete and chemically valid molecules. Experiments show that DBMol effectively optimizes the Boltz-2 affinity proxy and generates molecules with strong predicted affinity and specificity under Boltz-2 evaluation. To reduce self-confirmation bias, we further evaluate generated molecules using held-out metrics, including AF3-based evaluation. DBMol substantially improves pocket coverage while maintaining molecular diversity over unconditional generation, and is competitive under held-out metrics despite the absence of reference-ligand supervision. These results support the promise of structure prediction models as effective optimization signals for de novo molecular design.

AI.tldr: DBMol is a structure predictor-guided framework for de novo small molecule design that alternates between gradient-based optimization of binding affinity using a structure prediction model (Boltz-2) and flow-matching projection to chemically valid molecules, achieving strong predicted affinity and specificity.
AI.motivation: Designing high-affinity small molecule ligands for specific protein pockets is a fundamental goal in drug discovery. Recent breakthroughs in structure prediction (AlphaFold-3, Boltz-2) enable accurate biomolecular interaction prediction, offering promise as foundation models for downstream tasks like binding affinity prediction—motivating their use as optimization signals for molecular design.
AI.method: DBMol formulates an alternating optimization and projection process: (1) Optimization stage—starts from an initial molecule and uses gradient-based optimization to improve pocket-specific interactions and predicted binding affinity via a structure prediction model (Boltz-2). (2) Projection stage—a flow-matching model maps the optimized molecular graph to discrete, chemically valid molecules.
AI.result: DBMol effectively optimizes the Boltz-2 affinity proxy, generating molecules with strong predicted affinity and specificity. It substantially improves pocket coverage while maintaining molecular diversity over unconditional generation, and is competitive under held-out metrics (including AF3-based evaluation) despite no reference-ligand supervision.
AI.conclusion: Structure prediction models show promise as effective optimization signals for de novo molecular design, supporting their integration into generative drug discovery pipelines.

title: Thermodynamics-Informed Input Reparameterization for Neural Prediction of Real-Fluid Thermodynamic Properties in Supercritical Combustion
summary: Real-fluid thermodynamic property evaluation is a major computational cost in supercritical combustion simulations. In the enthalpy-based pressure-correction formulation, the closure evaluates temperature T, density $ρ$, and compressibility coefficient $ψ$ from the solver state (h,p,Y) through enthalpy-temperature inversion and repeated real-fluid equation-of-state evaluations. Neural-network surrogates offer fixed-cost inference, but direct mapping from (h,p,Y) to $(T,ρ,ψ)$ must capture the enthalpy-temperature relation and non-ideal equation-of-state response, resulting in a complex regression problem. This work introduces a thermodynamics-informed input reparameterization strategy, termed target-aligned input reparameterization (TAIR). TAIR replaces the raw enthalpy coordinate of each property network with a target-matched thermodynamic coordinate: the temperature network uses a temperature estimate obtained by inverting a constant-$c_p$ ideal-gas mixture enthalpy approximation, whereas the density and compressibility networks use an ideal-gas density estimate. These algebraic transformations use only solver-available variables and species constants, guiding the networks to learn real-fluid departures from ideal-gas baselines rather than reconstructing the full closure from raw enthalpy. The method is assessed using supercritical methane-oxygen counterflow flame data against a raw-input baseline and target-inconsistent cross-reparameterization controls. TAIR reduces held-out RMSE by factors of about 1.5, 2.0, and 7.5 for T, $ρ$, and $ψ$, respectively. For an unseen strain-rate flame within the augmented thermodynamic envelope, the corresponding factors are 3.6, 14.5, and 6.0. The target-inconsistent controls perform worse, indicating that the gains arise from thermodynamically matched input design rather than generic preprocessing.

AI.tldr: A thermodynamics-informed input reparameterization (TAIR) replaces raw enthalpy inputs with target-matched thermodynamic coordinates in neural-network surrogates for real-fluid property evaluation, reducing RMSE by factors of 1.5-7.5 in supercritical combustion simulations.
AI.motivation: Real-fluid thermodynamic property evaluation is computationally expensive in supercritical combustion simulations, and direct neural-network mapping from (h,p,Y) to (T,ρ,ψ) involves a complex regression problem due to the enthalpy-temperature relation and non-ideal equation-of-state response.
AI.method: TAIR replaces raw enthalpy with target-aligned inputs: temperature network uses an estimate from constant-cp ideal-gas inversion; density and compressibility networks use ideal-gas density estimates. Networks learn real-fluid departures from ideal-gas baselines.
AI.result: TAIR reduces held-out RMSE by ~1.5× for T, ~2.0× for ρ, ~7.5× for ψ. On unseen strain-rate flames: 3.6×, 14.5×, and 6.0× improvements. Target-inconsistent controls perform worse, confirming gains come from thermodynamic matching.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamically matched input design substantially improves neural-network surrogate accuracy for real-fluid property evaluation over raw-input baselines.

title: Benchmarking Generalization in Financial Statement Fraud Detection: robust evaluation and novel tasks
summary: Financial statement fraud detection (FSFD) is crucial for market integrity but faces challenges from increasingly sophisticated schemes and under-utilized textual data in financial reports. Existing methods often rely on random data splits, leading to overoptimistic performance estimates that do not reflect real-world generalization to new companies or future periods. To address this recurring problem with the state of the art, we propose a robust FSFD framework leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to integrate both structured financial data and unstructured textual information from financial reports. We provide a more realistic evaluation through a novel and challenging benchmark task called Company-Isolated FSFD (CI-FSFD). We construct and make publicly available a comprehensive U.S. company dataset combining financial statements, summarized MD&A text, and fraud labels. Our approach achieves the best performance on the challenging CI-FSFD task, demonstrating the critical value of textual data and robust evaluation for reliable financial fraud detection.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an LLM-based FSFD framework that integrates structured and textual data, introduces a realistic Company-Isolated benchmark (CI-FSFD) to combat overoptimistic evaluation, and achieves state-of-the-art results on a new public U.S. dataset.
AI.motivation: Financial statement fraud detection suffers from overoptimistic performance due to random data splits that fail to reflect real-world generalization to unseen companies or future periods, and textual data in financial reports remains under-utilized.
AI.method: A robust FSFD framework using Large Language Models (LLMs) to combine structured financial data with unstructured text (summarized MD&A), plus a novel Company-Isolated benchmark (CI-FSFD) for realistic evaluation and a new public U.S. company dataset.
AI.result: The proposed approach achieves the best performance on the challenging CI-FSFD task, demonstrating the critical value of textual data and robust evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Integrating textual data via LLMs and adopting company-isolated evaluation are essential for reliable and generalizable financial fraud detection in practice.

title: Toward Auditable Fraud Detection: Combining Graph Features, Model Explanations, and Agentic Case Investigation
summary: Fraud detection systems must scale with rising transaction volume while remaining explainable and reviewable. We study a layered pipeline on the PaySim dataset that combines a gradient-boosted classifier, graph-derived structural features, an autoencoder-based anomaly signal, TreeSHAP explanations, and a bounded LLM investigation agent applied to cases the classifier scores uncertainly. Before any model comparison, we identify and remove a simulator-specific balance shortcut that would otherwise inflate baseline performance. After this correction, neither the graph features nor the anomaly signal improves Average Precision on the full test set. Both, however, rank fraud better within the subset of cases receiving intermediate baseline scores. In a controlled experiment with injected multi-account fraud rings, engineered structural features recover all injected test transactions, while the tabular baseline misses roughly a quarter of them. The investigation agent underperforms direct thresholding of the classifier it relies on, reaching 65.0% accuracy against 71.7% on a balanced 60-case sample, despite having access to model explanations, graph context, and retrieved reference cases. Of the eight decisions the agent changed, six replaced correct classifier outputs with errors, and it produced a coherent written rationale in each case. An exploratory disagreement-based escalation rule flagged two of these agent errors for human review without flagging any correct decision. We conclude that each component of a layered fraud system contributes only under specific conditions, and that a plausible rationale from an investigation agent is not evidence of a better decision.

AI.tldr: A study of a layered fraud detection pipeline on PaySim data finds that graph features and anomaly signals only help on intermediate-score cases and against injected fraud rings; an LLM investigation agent underperforms simple thresholding, and its rationales mask worse decisions.
AI.motivation: Fraud detection systems need to scale with transaction volume while remaining explainable and reviewable, motivating the study of a layered pipeline combining multiple ML components and an LLM agent.
AI.method: The pipeline combines gradient-boosted classifier, graph features, autoencoder anomaly signal, TreeSHAP explanations, and a bounded LLM agent applied to uncertain cases. A simulator-specific balance shortcut is identified and removed before evaluation. Controlled experiments with injected fraud rings are conducted.
AI.result: Graph features and anomaly signals don't improve overall Average Precision but help on intermediate-score cases and recover all injected fraud rings (vs. 75% for baseline). The LLM agent achieves 65.0% accuracy vs. 71.7% for direct thresholding; 6 of 8 changed decisions replaced correct outputs with errors, though an escalation rule flagged 2 errors without any false positives.
AI.conclusion: Each component of a layered fraud system contributes only under specific conditions, and a plausible rationale from an investigation agent does not guarantee a better decision.

title: GUIDED Network-Agnostic Feature Initialization for Spatial Transferability in GNN-based Models
summary: The Traffic Assignment Problem is a fundamental but computationally expensive component of transportation planning. While Graph Neural Networks have emerged as fast, data-driven surrogates, their practical deployment is severely constrained by a spatial generalization gap. Standard models rely on transductive feature initializations that tie travel demand to fixed network topologies, preventing seamless transfer to new urban environments. To overcome this structural limitation, this research proposes a network-agnostic initialization layer, termed Geometrically Unconstrained Inductive Demand EmbeDding (GUIDED). By injecting travel demand as a scalar attribute on auxiliary virtual links rather than as specific node features, this modular framework standardizes the input space regardless of network scale. Extensive experimental evaluation across multiple urban topologies demonstrates that a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network (HetGAT) model integrated with the proposed GUIDED layer maintains state-of-the-art predictive accuracy on single-network tasks, while demonstrating superior robustness to out-of-distribution demand patterns and maintaining a distinct performance advantage over the baseline even under severe data scarcity. Notably, the proposed feature initialization enables highly parameter-efficient domain adaptation for inter-network transfer learning without artificial input homogenization, establishing a robust foundation for truly inductive models. At the same time, the optimized scatter operations of the initialization layer yield an approximate 50% reduction in training time per epoch compared to the baseline approach. Furthermore, while demonstrated on vehicular traffic, this fundamental abstraction of spatial topology provides a versatile blueprint for generalized origin-destination spatial problems, such as freight logistics and multimodal network optimization.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes GUIDED, a network-agnostic initialization layer that injects travel demand via auxiliary virtual links rather than node features, enabling Graph Neural Networks to generalize across different urban traffic networks without retraining. When integrated with a HetGAT model, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, robustness to out-of-distribution demands, 50% training time reduction, and effective inter-network transfer learning.
AI.motivation: Graph Neural Network surrogates for the Traffic Assignment Problem suffer from a spatial generalization gap: standard transductive feature initializations tie travel demand to fixed network topologies, preventing seamless transfer to new urban environments.
AI.method: Proposes GUIDED (Geometrically Unconstrained Inductive Demand EmbeDding), a modular initialization layer that injects travel demand as scalar attributes on auxiliary virtual links rather than as specific node features, standardizing the input space regardless of network scale. Integrated with a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network (HetGAT).
AI.result: (1) Maintains state-of-the-art predictive accuracy on single-network tasks; (2) Superior robustness to out-of-distribution demand patterns; (3) Performance advantage even under severe data scarcity; (4) Enables parameter-efficient inter-network domain adaptation; (5) ~50% reduction in training time per epoch via optimized scatter operations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed GUIDED layer establishes a robust foundation for truly inductive Graph Neural Network models in transportation, and the fundamental abstraction of spatial topology provides a versatile blueprint for generalized origin-destination spatial problems beyond vehicular traffic, such as freight logistics and multimodal network optimization.

title: A Reinforcement-Learning-Augmented Liquid-Fueled Reactor Network Model for Predicting Lean Blowout in Gas Turbine Combustors
summary: This study introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for generating optimal liquid-fueled reactors to improve lean blowout (LBO) predictions in gas turbine combustors. Existing approaches for determining cluster boundaries rely on manual heuristics or distance-based metrics in the input space. In contrast, the proposed method is goal-oriented, explicitly accounting for the target metric (e.g., LBO prediction accuracy) during cluster formation. The framework employs a multi-stage clustering--classification strategy: an initial clustering step (e.g., $k$-means clustering) generates a large set of homogeneous micro-clusters, followed by an actor-critic RL agent that merges them into optimal reactor zones. The validation study, performed using a Jet-A mechanism (119 species, 841 reactions), shows the RL framework offers improved predictive fidelity compared to $k$-means and captures the correct LBO trends, while achieving substantial speedups relative to the high-fidelity computational model. Overall, the RL-driven approach demonstrates strong potential as a computationally efficient reduced-order modeling technique that can complement high-fidelity simulations for rapid design-space exploration.

AI.tldr: A reinforcement learning framework optimizes cluster merging for liquid-fueled reactors, improving lean blowout prediction accuracy and speed in gas turbine combustors compared to traditional methods like k-means.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for determining cluster boundaries rely on manual heuristics or distance-based metrics in the input space, which are suboptimal for predicting target metrics like LBO.
AI.method: Multi-stage clustering–classification strategy: initial k-means clustering generates micro-clusters, then an actor-critic RL agent merges them into optimal reactor zones, explicitly accounting for the target metric (LBO prediction accuracy).
AI.result: Validation with Jet-A mechanism (119 species, 841 reactions) shows RL framework offers improved predictive fidelity over k-means, captures correct LBO trends, and achieves substantial speedups relative to high-fidelity computational models.
AI.conclusion: The RL-driven approach is a computationally efficient reduced-order modeling technique that can complement high-fidelity simulations for rapid design-space exploration.

title: Real-time optimal control with shallow recurrent decoder networks
summary: Controlling dynamical systems in real-time across multiple scenarios is critical to enabling adaptive control strategies, ensuring stability and efficiency. However, to tailor control actions in response to varying scenarios, traditional optimal control problems typically require several system simulations, which are often computationally demanding due to the high-dimensionality of the underlying spatio-temporal dynamics. In this work, we exploit SHallow REcurrent Decoder networks-based Reduced Order Modeling (SHRED-ROM) to synthesize a real-time closed-loop controller for high-dimensional and parametric dynamics, relying solely on limited state sensor readings. After training the model on a few optimal examples given by an expert demonstrator, SHRED-ROM mimics the expert behavior with effective distributed control actions in new scenarios, alleviating the curse of dimensionality. Moreover, a sensor forecaster is synthesized and used to close the loop at the latent level, thus efficiently mitigating possible sensor failures or delays. The performance of the proposed optimal control strategy is finally assessed on three challenging high-dimensional cases dealing with either parametric density control or fluid flow control.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes SHRED-ROM, a reduced-order modeling framework using shallow recurrent decoder networks, to synthesize real-time closed-loop controllers for high-dimensional parametric dynamical systems. It mimics expert demonstrations using limited sensor data, employs a latent-level sensor forecaster for robustness, and demonstrates effectiveness on density and fluid flow control problems.
AI.motivation: Traditional optimal control for high-dimensional spatio-temporal dynamics requires computationally expensive system simulations across multiple scenarios. The goal is to enable real-time adaptive control strategies that are efficient, stable, and robust to sensor failures or delays.
AI.method: SHRED-ROM (SHallow REcurrent Decoder-based Reduced Order Modeling) is used to synthesize a closed-loop controller. The model is trained on a few expert-demonstrated optimal examples, then mimics expert behavior using only limited state sensor readings. A sensor forecaster is additionally built to close the loop at the latent level, mitigating sensor failures/delays.
AI.result: The proposed control strategy is assessed on three challenging high-dimensional cases: parametric density control and fluid flow control. It effectively alleviates the curse of dimensionality and achieves real-time control with distributed actions.
AI.conclusion: SHRED-ROM enables real-time closed-loop control for high-dimensional parametric dynamics using limited sensor data, reducing computational burden while maintaining robustness against sensor issues.

title: Riemannian Deep Learning:Modules, Networks, and Geometries
comment: PhD thesis, University of Trento. The presentation has revised some typos in the previous published papers
summary: Deep neural networks on manifold-valued representations have attracted growing interest, but many basic components remain tied to specific manifolds, rely on Euclidean approximations, or require costly and numerically fragile geometric operations. This thesis develops a unified framework for Riemannian deep learning from three complementary perspectives: reusable neural modules, manifold-specific network architectures, and the design of underlying geometries. It generalizes batch normalization from Euclidean spaces and individual manifolds to broad classes of Lie groups and gyrogroups, and extends multinomial logistic regression from Euclidean space to SPD manifolds and then to general Riemannian manifolds. It further develops neural networks for several important geometric representations, including an unconstrained model of hyperbolic space, Busemann-based hyperbolic learning, and full-rank correlation matrices. Finally, it introduces adaptive and computationally efficient Riemannian metrics on SPD manifolds, including learnable Log-Euclidean geometries and fast, stable Cholesky-based geometries. The proposed methods are supported by theoretical analysis and validated through numerical experiments and applications in vision, signal processing, graph learning, and genomics.

AI.tldr: This thesis develops a unified framework for Riemannian deep learning, covering reusable neural modules (generalized batch normalization and logistic regression), manifold-specific architectures (hyperbolic and correlation matrix networks), and efficient metric designs (learnable Log-Euclidean and Cholesky-based geometries on SPD manifolds), validated across vision, signal processing, graph learning, and genomics.
AI.motivation: Existing deep learning on manifolds is limited by manifold-specific designs, Euclidean approximations, or costly/numerically fragile geometric operations. A unified, principled framework is needed to generalize key neural components across diverse Riemannian geometries.
AI.method: Proposes a tripartite framework: (1) reusable modules by generalizing batch normalization to Lie groups/gyrogroups and logistic regression to SPD and general Riemannian manifolds; (2) manifold-specific architectures including unconstrained hyperbolic models, Busemann-based hyperbolic learning, and full-rank correlation matrix networks; (3) metric design via learnable Log-Euclidean and fast stable Cholesky-based metrics on SPD manifolds.
AI.result: The proposed methods are supported by theoretical analysis and validated through numerical experiments across vision, signal processing, graph learning, and genomics.
AI.conclusion: A unified Riemannian deep learning framework is feasible and effective, generalizing core neural components across manifolds while introducing computationally efficient and adaptive geometric tools, with broad application success.

title: Staypoint Detection from Noisy Trajectory Data [Experiment Paper]
summary: Detecting staypoints from raw trajectory data is fundamental to numerous spatial computing applications. This process transforms raw numeric sequences of geolocations into semantically meaningful locations, such as homes, workplaces, or restaurants. Despite its importance for semantic trajectory analysis, staypoint detection lacks standard benchmarks, and existing algorithms have never been systematically evaluated. This gap persists because no publicly available datasets provide both raw individual trajectories and ground-truth staypoint annotations. This benchmark paper addresses this limitation with two key contributions: (1) we introduce 16 large-scale simulated datasets capturing thousands of agents with annotated staypoints across varying trajectory noise levels, and (2) we evaluate nine staypoint detection algorithms-including both state-of-the-art and novel methods-to analyze their robustness to noise. Our evaluation reveals that existing state-of-the-art algorithms perform poorly under realistic noise conditions. Conversely, our proposed unsupervised methods yield substantial improvements, while supervised approaches drastically outperform existing baselines. While these results are very promising, these datasets and methods are only meant as starting points for future research in staypoint detection.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 16 large-scale simulated datasets with annotated staypoints and evaluates 9 detection algorithms, finding that existing methods perform poorly under noise while proposed unsupervised and supervised approaches achieve substantial improvements.
AI.motivation: Staypoint detection lacks standard benchmarks and publicly available datasets with ground-truth annotations, and existing algorithms have never been systematically evaluated.
AI.method: The authors created 16 large-scale simulated datasets with thousands of agents and annotated staypoints across varying trajectory noise levels, then evaluated 9 staypoint detection algorithms (including state-of-the-art, novel unsupervised, and supervised methods) for robustness to noise.
AI.result: Existing state-of-the-art algorithms perform poorly under realistic noise conditions. Proposed unsupervised methods yield substantial improvements, and supervised approaches drastically outperform existing baselines.
AI.conclusion: The datasets and methods serve as starting points for future research in staypoint detection, highlighting the need for noise-robust approaches.

title: Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning in large language models. Yet, typical RLVR approaches fail on difficult problems: when a model cannot generate any correct solutions, it receives \textit{zero} learning signal. Providing privileged guidance during training, such as solution prefixes, can help overcome this learning cliff by steering the model towards {correct solutions with non-zero reward}. {We call these rollouts \textit{off-context}: they are generated from a training prompt that contains privileged guidance, while the target objective is defined by the original prompt without that guidance.} {We introduce} Off-Context GRPO (OC-GRPO), a minimally modified variant of GRPO that uses guided rollouts but applies an importance-corrected objective to steer the update back toward the original unguided objective, avoiding the mismatch that destabilizes uncorrected guided training. Empirically, our algorithm achieves a 3.9\% absolute improvement (13.8\% relative gain) over vanilla GRPO on average across standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks with negligible additional cost.

AI.tldr: OC-GRPO improves RLVR for LLMs by using privileged guidance (solution prefixes) during training to avoid zero reward signals on hard problems, with importance correction to prevent distribution mismatch, yielding 3.9% absolute improvement over GRPO.
AI.motivation: Typical RLVR approaches fail on difficult problems because when a model cannot generate any correct solutions, it receives zero learning signal (the "learning cliff").
AI.method: Off-Context GRPO (OC-GRPO) uses guided rollouts (privileged guidance like solution prefixes) during training to ensure non-zero reward, but applies an importance-corrected objective to keep the update aligned with the original unguided objective, preventing destabilization from the distribution mismatch.
AI.result: 3.9% absolute improvement (13.8% relative gain) over vanilla GRPO on average across standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with negligible additional cost.
AI.conclusion: OC-GRPO effectively addresses the zero-reward problem in RLVR for hard reasoning tasks by leveraging privileged guidance with proper correction, achieving significant gains without extra overhead.

title: CircuitKIT : Circuit Discovery, Evaluation, and Application Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability
summary: Circuit analysis can support not only model explanation but also downstream interventions such as pruning, editing, steering, and selective fine-tuning. However, conducting such analyses currently requires stitching together separate implementations for discovery, evaluation, and intervention, as well as hand-authoring the contrastive prompts required by many discovery methods. This fragmentation makes methods difficult to compare and limits their application beyond canonical tasks. We introduce CircuitKIT, a source-available library that connects the circuit-analysis workflow through a typed, serializable representation. CircuitKIT provides a suite of discovery algorithms, declarative interfaces for mapping structured data into discovery tasks, complementary circuit diagnostics, and downstream application modules. Together, these components provide common infrastructure for conducting and comparing circuit analyses. The library, examples, notebooks, and documentation are released at https://github.com/Lexsi-Labs/CircuitKIT .

AI.tldr: CircuitKIT is a source-available library that unifies the circuit-analysis workflow with a typed, serializable representation, providing discovery algorithms, declarative data interfaces, diagnostics, and intervention modules to streamline and standardize circuit analysis.
AI.motivation: Current circuit analysis requires stitching together separate implementations for discovery, evaluation, and intervention, along with hand-authoring contrastive prompts. This fragmentation hinders method comparison and limits application beyond canonical tasks.
AI.method: CircuitKIT connects the circuit-analysis workflow via a typed, serializable representation, offering a suite of discovery algorithms, declarative interfaces for mapping structured data into discovery tasks, complementary circuit diagnostics, and downstream application modules for intervention.
AI.result: The library provides common infrastructure for conducting and comparing circuit analyses, with examples, notebooks, and documentation released publicly.
AI.conclusion: CircuitKIT reduces fragmentation in circuit analysis by providing a unified, extensible framework for discovery, diagnostics, and intervention, enabling easier comparison and broader application of methods.

title: ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack
summary:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is rapidly advancing the reasoning capabilities of language models, yet the optimization layer that converts reward feedback into weight-space updates remains poorly understood. Building on our prior analysis (Zhu et al., 2025), we study this missing layer through the singular structure of model weights and identify spectral inheritance: RLVR can reuse the base model's weight spectra while acquiring new behavior through changes in the associated input and output singular frames.
  We operationalize spectral inheritance as Isospectral Optimization (ISO), an RLVR-native, fixed-spectrum optimization framework with complementary offline and online instantiations. Offline, ISO-Merger combines the frame changes of shared-base specialists into a single fixed-spectrum model, requiring no post-merge data, rollouts, gradient updates, or on-policy distillation (OPD). It recovers complementary specialist capabilities and achieves the strongest aggregate performance among the compared data-free merging methods. Online, ISO-Optimizer applies a chosen base optimizer, including AdamW and Muon, to the frame variables while keeping the base spectra fixed. Across reasoning and coding tasks ranging from 1.5B to 8B parameters, ISO-Optimizer improves accuracy in the reported runs and reaches matched scores with substantially fewer training steps. On Qwen3-8B-Base, AdamW reaches an aggregate accuracy of 0.495 after 270 training steps. ISO-AdamW reaches the same accuracy after only 100 training steps and improves further to 0.509 after 210 training steps. Together, ISO offers a concrete answer to RLVR's missing optimization layer: rather than inheriting pre-training optimization wholesale, design post-training around the structure of reward-driven adaptation: inherit the spectrum, optimize the frames.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Isospectral Optimization (ISO), a framework for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) that preserves the base model's weight spectra while optimizing only the input/output singular frames. ISO has offline (ISO-Merger for merging specialists) and online (ISO-Optimizer, achieving faster convergence on reasoning/coding tasks) instantiations, demonstrating that RLVR post-training should inherit spectra and optimize frames.
AI.motivation: The optimization layer that converts reward feedback into weight-space updates in RLVR remains poorly understood; the authors aim to uncover the missing structure of how RLVR adapts model weights.
AI.method: The authors identify spectral inheritance through singular structure analysis and operationalize it as Isospectral Optimization (ISO), a fixed-spectrum framework with two instantiations: ISO-Merger (offline merging of frame changes from shared-base specialists) and ISO-Optimizer (online optimization of frame variables with base spectra fixed, using standard optimizers like AdamW and Muon).
AI.result: ISO-Merger achieves strongest aggregate performance among compared data-free merging methods. ISO-Optimizer reaches target accuracy in fewer steps (e.g., on Qwen3-8B-Base, ISO-AdamW reaches accuracy 0.495 in 100 steps vs AdamW's 270 steps, and improves to 0.509 by 210 steps).
AI.conclusion: RLVR's missing optimization layer is best addressed by inheriting the base model's spectrum and optimizing the singular frames, rather than wholesale inheriting pre-training optimization.

title: Provable diffusion-based posterior sampling for linear inverse problems via DDIM
summary: Diffusion-based methods have achieved remarkable empirical success in solving inverse problems. However, many existing posterior samplers either lack rigorous theoretical guarantees or incur substantial computational overhead. We propose a simple and efficient algorithm, called \pddim, for solving linear inverse problems with diffusion priors via a DDIM-type sampler. Our method requires only lightweight, coordinate-wise modifications to the standard DDIM update, while explicitly incorporating the measurement model. The key idea is to perform posterior sampling separately along each singular direction of the measurement operator: for each direction, the sampler follows the learned diffusion prior when the observation signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is below the corresponding diffusion SNR, and switches to a calibrated measurement-based predictor otherwise. We prove that the proposed sampler converges to the Bayesian posterior conditioned on the measurements. Empirical results show that the proposed sampler performs favorably against existing diffusion-based posterior samplers across a range of image restoration tasks, achieving the best performance on the majority of evaluation metrics considered. Overall, our results convert posterior sampling for noisy linear inverse problems to simple coordinate-wise DDIM updates, yielding an efficient, easy-to-implement algorithm with provable posterior consistency.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes PDDIM, a DDIM-type sampler for solving linear inverse problems with diffusion priors that performs lightweight coordinate-wise modifications to incorporate measurement models, switching between prior-based and measurement-based updates based on signal-to-noise ratio comparisons along each singular direction. The method is proven to converge to the Bayesian posterior and achieves state-of-the-art performance on image restoration tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based posterior samplers for inverse problems either lack rigorous theoretical guarantees or incur substantial computational overhead.
AI.method: The method performs posterior sampling separately along each singular direction of the measurement operator. For each direction, it follows the learned diffusion prior when the observation SNR is below the diffusion SNR, and switches to a calibrated measurement-based predictor otherwise. This is implemented via simple coordinate-wise modifications to the standard DDIM update.
AI.result: The proposed sampler achieves favorable performance against existing diffusion-based posterior samplers across a range of image restoration tasks, attaining the best results on most evaluation metrics considered.
AI.conclusion: Posterior sampling for noisy linear inverse problems can be converted to simple coordinate-wise DDIM updates, yielding an efficient, easy-to-implement algorithm with provable posterior consistency.
